Read/screened bodies; the Nov 3 generic-card description supplies no dated primary UI work and the Nov 5 type-scale post is about context and reading size. Its illustrated pavilion is not a UI screenshot. The older gap remains.

Checked every entry in the public Atom feed and matching author index (12 entries, no next page), including published and updated dates. The newest entry and update are Aug 31. No publications or revisions in the planned Oct 19–Nov 9 overlap; no eligible primary work to open.

Full RSS bodies with publication dates cross-checked against the paginated writing index for the period July 24–August 23. Eight in-window items screened: July 29 and 30; Aug 5, 6, 12, 13, 19, 20. Four weekly link roundups and four original articles; the July 30 CSS card is a didactic contrast with an existing design system and not a dated sample of a public product. The August essays cover motion instructions, context loading and a skills collection, not independent viewed product examples.

Read creative/video archive pages 2–3 and two dated case texts (Ilim, Aug 17; VILKA/Biocodex, Aug 14). Archive covers selected video listings and is not the complete publisher archive. Actual motion and several relevant case works remain unreviewed; keep original boundary.

Screened public July/August archive pages, including July pages 4–5 and August pages 1–4. The July 24 page boundary overlaps an unchecked previous page; some August entries are excerpts. Aug 7 raccoon prototype describes a concrete rendering bug, not a confirmed repeated visual default. No complete review of relevant primary work; keep the boundary.

visuals.label: gaga-img
visuals.visible_observation: A black goose mascot wears a hat and transparent raincoat under a saturated yellow umbrella. Backlit drops and out-of-focus street lights frame the upturned beak. The recurring yellow reinforces the wet-weather footwear premise; the shot does not depict a human domestic scene.

visuals.label: alfa-img
visuals.visible_observation: Editorial cover with white Cyrillic headline on a darkened behind-the-scenes photograph. A monitor displays suspended colored strips; stands and cables remain visible. This is the publisher cover, not a film frame.

visuals.label: koch-img
visuals.visible_observation: A perspective drawing of an open reading pavilion sets a standing lectern beside a seated desk and open book. The image illustrates two reading contexts and does not show the website type scale.

visuals.label: levis-img
visuals.visible_observation: The brand hero is a two-row grid of portraits against alternating red, pink, green and blue backgrounds. Ribbed knit caps, thick scarves and shaggy cushions foreground the collection texture. This is campaign photography, not a stop-motion frame.

visuals.label: levis-film-img
visuals.visible_observation: The left portion shows the white shaggy yeti in a red sweater beside puppets in a wood-paneled cabin, with warm lamps, small colored lights and a textured rug. The right portion is a separate behind-the-scenes view of a miniature snowy cabin, trees and studio lighting. The sweater and fur textures carry the campaign idea.

visuals.label: elf-img
visuals.visible_observation: Three puppets fill a doorway against deep blue. Orange yarn buns, yellow braids, red earmuffs and contrasting knit clothes make the figures distinct; the miniature turquoise e.l.f. bottle is visible beside the camera prop. The shared material vocabulary supports character differentiation.

visuals.label: bound-img
visuals.visible_observation: A pale lavender field frames a central collage of Dolly Parton and Tim Curry with a white notification overlay, hand-drawn pictograms, dark-outlined peach buttons and a cream footer. The handwritten logo and separate italic footer links do not form a high-contrast serif hero on cream with a clay accent.

editorial_review.decision: No admission: recency and independence do not substitute for a repeated concrete combination functioning as a default.
editorial_review.independence: GAGA/Lenta, Levi’s/Blinkink, e.l.f./Apartment D and Bound are distinct origins and families. Retail hero and film still share the Levi’s campaign; the two Creative Bloq articles are discovery routes, not additional origin counts.
editorial_review.counterevidence: The e.l.f. and Levi’s stills deliberately tie visible fibers, color and character materials to different briefs; holiday stop-motion and saturated accents are conventions. The Bound screenshot uses pink/cream in subordinate roles and collage as hierarchy; not a generic cream-serif-clay hero.

watchlist_decisions.VNS-W001: No second independent recent domestic-ad work with the three features. GAGA is a rainwear mascot; independent toy characters from the seasonal work are intentionally stylized. No film movement assessed.
watchlist_decisions.VNS-W002: Targeted query yielded older analyses and generic font discussion. Bound has a creamy footer and contrasting letter styles, but not the target role combination.
watchlist_decisions.VNS-W003: Koch’s July card text concerns white fill, shadow and radius without side accents. November prose has no inspected product witness. No second dated example from an independent family.

access_limits: Devialet still timed out after two retries. Its campaign text was read; no viewed Devialet image claimed.
Sostav video category and Willison archive had gaps or excerpts; neither checkpoint advanced. Motion, interactive states, and population frequency were not established.
C01–C04 were not due for exact Git checks; no new evidence justified an early one.
